model_context: Fresh Codex exec process for every decision; only that trial's public task, initial feedback, previous answers and feedback are replayed.
feedback_difference: Only the counterexample arm receives the native checker's violating_pair for a failed preservation test. Constraint errors are identical in both arms.
scoring: Repairs must preserve all original equivalences, retain the required separation, and pass the identified native preservation checker. Impossible answers are scored by independent exhaustive enumeration of all 15 partitions.
held_out_meaning: Test tasks use operation conjugacy families absent from development tasks. No claim that the underlying mathematics or tasks were absent from model training.
limits: One model/configuration, one repetition, twelve small paired test tasks; descriptive pilot only.
The four-object task has very few legal repairs, so ceiling effects can hide any feedback benefit.
Every selected initial grouping has exactly one distinct same-group pair. Knowing it fails already determines that pair; the witness explicitly highlights information inferable from the task.
Codex CLI settings and inherited global instructions are part of the tested harness; requested settings are not proof of a server model snapshot.
The Lean proof covers preservation and returned witnesses. Merge constraints and impossibility scoring are separately tested Python code.
Equal decision budgets do not imply equal tokens or computation; counterexample feedback contains additional explicit feedback text.
